why: u:t/sys:1/star:0 exploded 20000 years ago with 1.0e44 J; the blast is in its pressure-driven snowplough phase, 32.7 pc across and moving at 287 km/s.

stand_ins: only hydrogen's recombination lines so far: oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur and helium lines (the teal cores and red edges) come from the line-strength grid in O4
the white dwarf's ionising light is held at its birth temperature; its cooling (and the nebula dimming with it) comes when the remnant track gives the cooling curve
the shell is uniform: no clumps or density gradient in the surroundings
why: Shed by u:t/sys:0/star:0 4000 years ago; the shell coasts out at 19 km/s and is now 0.16 pc across.
The white dwarf (100000 K) gives 1.6e46 ionising photons a second, fewer than the 4.2e46 recombinations the dense young shell would need: only its inner part glows.
2 faint rings outside it are earlier puffs of the giant's slow wind, 966 years apart: the shed layers.
a close companion squeezes the outflow at the waist, so it blows out two lobes 3.6 times longer than wide.
